epic.title: compat(app): Electron app lifecycle, single-instance, paths and process shim over host-owned lifecycle
epic.body:
## Scope
Electron `app` module (115 members: 75 methods, 30 events, 10 properties), `CommandLine` (5), `Dock` (11, macOS), `process` shim (29). Live today: `app.whenReady/isReady/quit/on/off/removeListener`, `ready` and `window-all-closed` events, `process.type='browser'`, `process.versions.electron='0.0.1'` (KEL-72). Everything else is TARGET.

## Corpus demand (resolved call sites, 2026-10-06)
whenReady/ready, window-all-closed, quit, exit, getPath (Zettlr ~40 sites, draw.io 3), getVersion, requestSingleInstanceLock + second-instance (both apps), open-file (Zettlr), before-quit/will-quit, activate, relaunch (Zettlr), isPackaged, setAppUserModelId, disableHardwareAcceleration, process.argv/defaultApp parsing (draw.io).

## Maturity ladder (exit criteria)
- L0: every `app` member exists with a typed `KELD-COMPAT` error for unsupported calls (never a silent no-op).
- L1: electron-quick-start and draw.io boot through `whenReady`, `activate`, `window-all-closed`, `quit` on macOS.
- L2: ordering sequences `before-quit → per-window close → will-quit → quit` (and the `quitAndInstall` inversion) pass conformance entries citing the pinned v44.4.5 `app.md` sentences, with negative controls; `second-instance` delivered exactly once with typed argv/cwd.
- L3: draw.io and Zettlr primary workflows exercise the family under `keld dev` (KEL-74 records, authority profile printed).

## Linear owners consumed
KEL-72 (lifecycle facade), KEL-142 (@keld/api lifecycle/channel), KEL-139/KEL-143 (Ready and generation recovery semantics), KEL-75 (role spawn facts), KEL-78 (strict child environment), KEL-19/KEL-15 (config/bundle emission), KEL-96 (keld dev exit codes).

## Design facts fixed by research (two refuters)
- Host `Ready` is emitted today on the first host-created window's navigation; Electron's `ready` fires before any window exists. Ready must be re-based to "host initialized, window module available" while keeping the wire enum unchanged (KEL-237 cells stay valid) and pairing the re-base with KEL-143 recovery semantics.
- Quit is one-shot and uncancelable today; Electron's cancelable `before-quit`/`will-quit` and renderer `beforeunload` need a two-phase, host-owned protocol. `app.exit(code)` cannot be `process.exit` (the supervisor would recover the role); it is a host Call.
- The strict Bun child receives only `KELD_APP_LINK` and log sinks, so single-instance, second-instance argv/cwd/additionalData, open-file/open-url, path roots and OS registrations are host-owned and delivered as typed events or boot facts.
- Protocol-client and login-item registration are build-time declarations materialised by packaging; the facade reports false with a diagnostic until an emitter exists.
- `app.commandLine.*` is a facade-local self-consistent store with a one-time dev warning (arbitrary Chromium flags are documented-never).

## Platform lanes
macOS first (Dock, open-file/open-url, activate, Handoff APIs are macOS-tagged: 44 members); Windows (jump lists, AppUserModelId, toast activator: 20 members); Linux (badge, desktop name: 4 members). `before-quit/will-quit/quit` are not emitted on Windows shutdown — documented ▲.

tickets.title: feat(app): two-phase host-owned quit with before-quit/will-quit cancellation and app.exit as a host Call
tickets.what_to_build: Make quit two-phase: the facade emits `before-quit` locally for facade-initiated quit, then asks the host to close all windows through the cancelable per-window close protocol (F02), then emits `will-quit`, then issues the existing Quit Call. `app.exit(7)` exits the host session with status 7 under `keld dev` (CLI contract) and never triggers a restart
`quitAndInstall` ordering is split by facade × platform as documented (see F09)
negative_controls: Removing the cancellation path makes the preventDefault entry fail
Implementing app.exit as process.exit triggers supervisor recovery and fails the exit entry

decision_tickets.title: Where does `userData` live under the strict profile: guard grant root or KEL-78 role-private container?
decision_tickets.question: Electron apps (electron-store, electron-log) write under `app.getPath("userData")` with raw `node:fs`. Making `userData` a generated `app.fs.*` grant root contradicts KEL-78 (a guard grant is not OS containment and a JS shim cannot mediate native code). Choose one owner: (a) place `userData`/`logs` inside the KEL-78 reviewed role-private container so `node:fs` works by OS containment with no guard grant, or (b) a `node:fs`-over-FsBroker facade for strict roles. Which, and what does `keld migrate` print for apps that need the other?

decision_tickets.title: Which owner emits bundle declarations (Info.plist CFBundleURLTypes, .desktop, MSIX) for protocol-client and login-item registration?
decision_tickets.question: Protocol-client and login-item registration are build-time declarations. keld-pack is a name-only enum today and KEL-19 may or may not include bundle emission. Confirm the owner and the `keld.config.ts` fields (KEL-15) before F01-T6 can be promoted beyond "false with diagnostic". This is a permission-model + KEL-15 schema gate.

yagni.reason: Conformance-first invariant for the lifecycle the proof exercises: ready-before-window (drawio electron.js:987 creates its window inside whenReady), window-all-closed (:2112), activate (:2127), before-quit (:2106). Slice: macOS entries for those four; park will-finish-launching on Windows/Linux.

Slice only: host-initiated quit must not bypass the per-window veto — draw.io's macOS menu has role 'quit' (:2042) and tracks Cmd+Q via before-quit (:2106) with every close vetoed (:947-963); a one-shot host quit past a dirty window is silent data loss on the scored unsaved-prompt contract. No resolved call site in either corpus app for commandLine.*, enableSandbox() (commented out at drawio :691), setAsDefaultProtocolClient or setLoginItemSettings (grep of both clones: zero hits).

`import ... from 'electron'` must resolve in app code and inside node_modules packages (electron-log :9, electron-updater :17, electron-store :20, electron-context-menu :22). Boot-fact half duplicates F01-T4.

ambiguity_laundering.claim: [fact] drawio electron.js:30 'store = new Store();' at top level; :58 app.getPath('userData') pre-ready — 'draw.io constructs electron-store at module top level and calls app.getPath('userData') pre-ready'.
ambiguity_laundering.problem: Half wrong against the source. Line 58 is inside detectInitialAdaptiveColorsDefault(), which is invoked from inside app.whenReady().then (≈:991) — post-ready — and sits in its own try/catch. `new Store()` at :30 is wrapped in try/catch (:28-36) with `store = null` as fallback, so a failing constructor degrades silently instead of breaking boot. The only pre-ready userData dependence is inside electron-store, which the same ticket lists as [unknown].
ambiguity_laundering.fix: FACT: Store is constructed at module top level inside try/catch; failure yields store=null (settings silently not persisted). FACT: the direct app.getPath('userData') call at :58 runs after ready. FACT: process.argv/env/platform are read at top level (:75-79, :164). UNKNOWN: whether electron-store/electron-log call app.getPath/getName/getVersion at construction — settled by PANEL-P3. The decision stands on the documented top-level contract plus that unknown.

ambiguity_laundering.claim: 'Pair the semantics with KEL-143 recovery (a successor generation receives Ready again with the same meaning)'; 'keep KEL-237 cells valid (no wire change)'.
ambiguity_laundering.problem: Presents a future KEL-143 artifact as the thing to pair with, while KEL-143 is Backlog and successor-generation Ready replay is already implemented in keld-core (app_session.rs:5087; test 'G2 Ready replay' at :7452). 'Cells stay valid' is an untested inference from 'the wire enum is unchanged'.
ambiguity_laundering.fix: FACT: keld-core replays Ready to a recovered generation today. INFERENCE: re-basing the emission point keeps the when-ready cell green — verify by running it. BLOCKER (named): 're-adopt the surviving window' depends on KEL-143 (Backlog).

hidden_coupling.coupling: Ready re-base ↔ recovery ↔ window adoption. Ready is emitted on NavigationReady today and is already replayed to a recovered generation; F02-T2 adds a transitional 'first new BrowserWindow() adopts the host-created primary window until F01-T2 lands'. Changing the emission point silently changes what the replayed Ready means in generation ≥2 (a window exists) and makes the adoption shim dead or wrong; F01-T2's AC1/AC3 already contradict each other on this.
hidden_coupling.fix: One atom 'who creates window #1 and what Ready means per generation', owned by F01-T2; edge F02-T2 ← F01-T2 and delete the adoption shim from F02-T2 (two mechanisms for one fact).

decision_packets.decision: How a quit request (Cmd+Q, app.quit, quitAndInstall) is sequenced against per-window close vetoes so that before-quit, per-window close, window-all-closed and will-quit match Electron 44.4.5 with two vetoing windows, and which AppKit termination reply the host uses to do it.
facts: FACT: Electron v44.4.5 overrides NSApplication terminate: and calls Browser::Quit(); the code comment says termination proceeds if all windows close and a cancelled window close aborts it (shell/browser/mac/electron_application.mm at v44.4.5, fetched 2026-10-06).
FACT: neither electron_application.mm nor electron_application_delegate.mm at v44.4.5 contains applicationShouldTerminate or any NSTerminate reply (grep of the fetched files, 2026-10-06).
FACT: Browser::Quit sets is_quitting_ from the before-quit result, then calls NotifyAndShutdown if there are no windows, otherwise WindowList::CloseAllWindows (shell/browser/browser.cc at v44.4.5).
FACT: CloseAllWindows snapshots the window list, reverses it on macOS, and calls Close() on every window without re-checking the quitting flag (shell/browser/window_list.cc at v44.4.5).
FACT: a close-event preventDefault calls WindowList::WindowCloseCancelled, and Browser::OnWindowCloseCancelled then sets is_quitting_ to false (native_window.cc and browser.cc at v44.4.5).

FACT: Browser::OnWindowAllClosed emits will-quit via NotifyAndShutdown when quitting, and otherwise emits window-all-closed (browser.cc at v44.4.5); app.md says that after Cmd+Q or app.quit the window-all-closed event 'would not be emitted'.

research.summary: Census: 160 members (app 115 = 75 methods/30 events/10 properties; CommandLine 5; Dock 11; process 29). Keld today implements a 5-member slice live (app.whenReady/isReady/quit/on/off + ready and window-all-closed events, process.type/process.versions.electron shims) over keld_ipc LIFECYCLE_CHANNEL=3 {Ready, LastWindowClosed, Quit}; everything else in the family is TARGET, and keld-native lists deeplink/autostart/dock as names only. Corpus demand ranks: whenReady/ready, window-all-closed, quit, exit, getPath (Zettlr 40 call sites, draw.io 3), getVersion, requestSingleInstanceLock+second-instance (both apps), open-file (Zettlr 20 sites, draw.io 1), before-quit/will-quit, activate, relaunch (Zettlr), focus/show (Zettlr), isPackaged, setAppUserModelId, disableHardwareAcceleration, process.defaultApp/argv parsing (draw.io). Four design-changing facts: (1) [fact] host Ready is currently signalled on NavigationReady of a host-created window (crates/keld-core/src/app_session.rs:3900), while Electron's ready fires before any window exists — BrowserWindow compat needs Ready re-based. (2) [fact] Quit is a one-shot correlated Call with no veto; Electron before-quit/will-quit preventDefault and beforeunload cancellation (Zettlr depends on it) need a two-phase host protocol; app.exit(code) cannot be process.exit because the supervisor recovers nonzero Bun exits with a fresh generation and re-sends Ready (arch 06 §1) and treats status-zero post-ready exit as KELD-RUNTIME-012. (3) [fact] the strict Bun child receives only KELD_APP_LINK + log sinks, so single-instance lock, second-instance argv/cwd/additionalData, open-file/open-url, getPath roots and OS registrations (protocol client, login items, dock) must be host-owned and delivered as typed events/calls; research 186 row 2 already classifies the handoff tuple as untrusted input. (4) [fact] protocol-client and login-item registration are build-time declarations (Info.plist CFBundleURLTypes, .desktop, MSIX uap:Protocol) and v0 has no .app/plist/MSIX emitter (keld-auth rung 2), so the facade must return false with a diagnostic rather than a silent true. commandLine.* is on the never list (arbitrary Chromium flags) and becomes a facade-local no-op store with a one-time dev warning. Six atoms below; all labelled; unknowns kept explicit.

decisions.question: What does host `Ready` mean once BrowserWindow is app-created? Today Ready is emitted on AppWindowEvent::NavigationReady of a host-created window; Electron `ready` fires once after the main process's first event-loop tick, before any window exists, and apps create windows inside whenReady.
decisions.proposed_answer: Re-base LifecycleEvent::Ready to 'host initialized, window module available, zero app windows' and move the first-window creation to the facade's `new BrowserWindow` (window module Call). Keep the wire enum unchanged (Ready=0x00) so KEL-237 cells stay valid; change only the host emission point. The existing LifecycleSession.window_opened/window_closed counter remains the LastWindowClosed owner (host-side registry count, not a facade-local count), which also fixes `activate(hasVisibleWindows)`. Type: task gated by a grilling on cold-start budget (window creation now waits for Bun start + HELLO; arch 01 §5 ≤300 ms cold→first paint must be re-measured, not assumed).

decisions.question: How do before-quit / will-quit / quit (with preventDefault and beforeunload cancellation) and app.exit(exitCode) map onto a host that owns windows and a supervisor that recovers Bun crashes?
decisions.proposed_answer: Make Quit two-phase and host-owned: (1) a host→app `QuitRequested{source}` Event for Cmd+Q / dock Quit / OS logoff / facade app.quit(); the facade emits before-quit, then host closes windows (running renderer beforeunload via the window module), then will-quit; any preventDefault or a beforeunload veto sends `QuitCancelled` back and the host stays alive; otherwise the facade sends the existing correlated `Quit` Call and emits `quit(exitCode)` on Reply. (2) Add a distinct `Exit{code}` Call: host replies, skips before-quit/will-quit, tears down with KEL-96 ordering and exits with `code`; the supervisor must classify the following Bun exit as host-authorized (same rule already used for status-zero after accepted Quit). `window-all-closed` must NOT be emitted during a quit-initiated close (host suppresses LastWindowClosed while a Quit is in flight). Type: grilling → approved spec amendment to KEL-96/KEL-139 Quit ordering (architecture change: crash ownership of an app-requested exit).
evidence: [fact] Electron app.md: app.quit 'Try to close all windows. The before-quit event will be emitted first ... This method guarantees that all beforeunload and unload event handlers are correctly executed.
